memory_candidates.content: When a downstream reader sums a parent record's field with its children's same-named field (e.g. total_tokens = sum(children.token_count) + parent.token_count), writing the parent's field to the true aggregate value double-counts. The correct convention -- confirmed by an independent, earlier fix to the same corpus -- is to write 0 (or the appropriate identity element) on the parent when children exist, leaving the children as the sole source of the aggregate. This is easy to get backwards because the field name ('token_count') and the task language ('document total') both suggest writing the real total; only executing the downstream reader against a real fixture (not just the writer's own output) surfaces the double-count.

A regression test that exercises a fallback/retry path (e.g. 'if filtered search returns zero results, retry unfiltered') can accidentally pass even when the primary fix under test is reverted, because the fallback masks the regression by finding the same result through an unrelated path. Guard against this by adding a decoy fixture that keeps the primary path's result count non-zero under BOTH the broken and fixed code, so the fallback never triggers and the test is forced to discriminate on the actual mechanism being tested. Discovered by literally reverting the fix and observing the test stay green -- a red-then-green demonstration is the only way to catch this class of false-positive test.
